messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings? Wait facilities param type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems odd: It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], but maybe it's a union of those strings or an array of strings? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." So likely we pass an array of strings specifying required facilities. But the type shows "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of string "Cafe"? Might be mis-specified. But we can pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

We need to call function thrice:

1. location: "New York, NY" facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA" facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL" facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We should call function each time. We'll produce separate calls.
